parameters.formDescription:
Remove unwanted people from your travel photos with AI.
AIで旅行写真から不要な人物を削除します。

Upload one or more photos to get started.
1枚以上の写真をアップロードしてください。

⚠️ For better results:
If a person occupies a large part of the photo or significantly overlaps with a person, animal, or object you want to keep, AI must reconstruct the hidden areas. The result may differ from the original photo.

⚠️ きれいに仕上げるためのポイント：
人物が写真の大部分を占めている場合や、残したい人物・動物・物に大きく重なっている場合、隠れている部分をAIが推測して生成するため、元の写真と異なる仕上がりになることがあります。

parameters.text:
{{ $json.preferred_language === 'ja'
  ? '以下の旅行写真を分析してください。回答内の position、description、scene_description は必ずすべて日本語で記述してください。英語で記述してはいけません。'
  : 'Analyze this travel photo. All position, description, and scene_description values must be written entirely in English.'
}}

Analyze this travel photo for real people who are physically present in the photographed scene.

Identify every visible real person in the scene, including partially visible people.

IMPORTANT CLASSIFICATION RULES:
- Count only real human beings who are physically present in the photographed scene.
- Do NOT count statues, sculptures, monuments, mannequins, dolls, figures, mascots, or human-shaped objects as people.
- Do NOT count people depicted in posters, signs, advertisements, billboards, screens, televisions, photographs, paintings, murals, printed materials, or other images within the photo.
- Do NOT count reflections unless you are confident the reflection belongs to a real person physically present in the photographed scene.
- If an object is ambiguous and you cannot confidently determine that it is a real person physically present in the scene, do NOT count it.
- A person riding a bicycle, motorcycle, scooter, wheelchair, or similar device IS a real person and should be counted.
- Objects associated with a person, such as bicycles, bags, strollers, or vehicles, must not themselves be counted as people.

OUTPUT LANGUAGE:
- Write the values of "position", "description", and "scene_description" in the language specified below.
- If the language is "ja", write these values in natural Japanese.
- If the language is "en", write these values in natural English.
- Do not translate JSON property names such as "people_count", "people", "id", "position", "description", or "scene_description".

PERSON DISTINGUISHING RULES:
The "position" and "description" fields will be used by an image editing AI to determine exactly which person should be kept or removed.

For "position":
- Describe the person's location using stable image coordinates such as left, center, right, foreground, background, upper, or lower.
- When people are close together, clearly distinguish their relative positions.
- Do not rely only on relationships such as "next to another person".

For "description":
- Prioritize stable visual features that clearly belong to that person.
- Prefer clothing color and type, pants or skirt color, hair color/style, mask, glasses, hat, bags, and other clearly attached accessories.
- Include approximate age category such as child or adult only when visually clear.
- Keep the description concise but sufficiently distinctive from every other detected person.

IMPORTANT FOR OVERLAPPING PEOPLE:
- Do NOT use a hand, arm, leg, gesture, pose, or other body part as a distinguishing feature if it overlaps another person or if ownership of that body part is uncertain.
- Do NOT attribute an overlapping hand, arm, leg, accessory, or object to a person unless you are confident it belongs to that person.
- When two or more people overlap, distinguish them primarily by clothing, hair, clearly attached accessories, and image position.
- Each person's description should contain enough independent visual information for an image editing model to locate that person without relying on another person's body parts.

OUTPUT LANGUAGE — STRICT REQUIREMENT:
The output language for all human-readable JSON values MUST be determined by the Language value below.

Language:
{{ $json.preferred_language }}

If Language is "ja":
- You MUST write "position", "description", and "scene_description" entirely in natural Japanese.
- Do NOT write any English sentences or English descriptions in these values.
- This requirement applies independently to EVERY photo processed.

If Language is "en":
- You MUST write "position", "description", and "scene_description" entirely in natural English.
- Do NOT write Japanese sentences in these values.

Before returning the JSON, verify that EVERY value of:
- "position"
- "description"
- "scene_description"

matches the specified Language.

Keep all JSON property names in English exactly as specified.

Return ONLY valid JSON with this structure:

{
  "people_count": 0,
  "people": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "position": "brief and precise description of where the person is in the image",
      "description": "brief visual description useful for distinguishing this person from others"
    }
  ],
  "scene_description": "brief description of the background and surroundings"
}

The people_count must exactly equal the number of objects in the people array.

If no real people are physically present, return:
{
  "people_count": 0,
  "people": [],
  "scene_description": "brief description of the background and surroundings"
}

Do not identify who any person is.
Do not use markdown.
Do not include any text outside the JSON.

parameters.prompt:
Remove only the real people who are physically present in this photo.

Remove every real person visible in the photographed scene.

IMPORTANT — PARTIALLY VISIBLE PEOPLE:
- A real person must be removed even if only a small part of their body is visible.
- Carefully inspect all four edges and corners of the image for cropped people.
- Remove partially cropped people entering from outside the frame.
- Remove visible human body parts belonging to real people in the photographed scene, including partial heads, faces, hair, shoulders, arms, hands, torsos, legs, and feet.
- Do not ignore a person because most of their body is outside the image.
- After editing, no part of any real person physically present in the photographed scene should remain visible.

When removing a real person:
- Reconstruct only the area actually obscured by that person.
- If the person is riding or directly using a bicycle, motorcycle, scooter, wheelchair, stroller, or similar object, remove that associated object together with the person.
- Remove objects being worn, carried, held, ridden, pushed, or pulled by the removed person when they clearly belong to that person's activity.

IMPORTANT PRESERVATION RULES:
- Do NOT remove statues, sculptures, monuments, mannequins, dolls, figures, mascots, or human-shaped objects.
- Do NOT remove people depicted in posters, signs, advertisements, billboards, screens, photographs, paintings, murals, or printed materials.
- Do NOT remove unrelated bicycles, vehicles, street furniture, fences, railings, signs, buildings, trees, objects, or background elements.
- Preserve all existing background structures and objects unless they are directly obscured by a person being removed.
- Reconstruct hidden background areas naturally based on the surrounding visible scene.
- Do not redesign, simplify, relocate, or replace existing background elements.
- Keep the original composition, perspective, lighting, colors, textures, shadows, and photographic appearance as closely as possible.

FINAL CHECK:
Before completing the edit, inspect the entire image again, especially all edges and corners, and ensure that no real person or cropped part of a real person physically present in the photographed scene remains visible.

The final image should be identical to the original photograph except that real people physically present in the scene, and objects directly associated with their activity when appropriate, are absent.

CRITICAL IDENTITY PRESERVATION RULE:
Every person listed in PEOPLE TO KEEP is a protected subject.

The protected subject must remain pixel-level as close to the original as possible.
Do NOT redraw, regenerate, retouch, beautify, reconstruct, or reinterpret the protected subject.

Specifically preserve exactly:
- face
- facial expression
- eyes
- mouth
- hairstyle
- skin
- body shape
- pose
- hands
- clothing
- accessories

Do not change the protected person's identity or appearance in any way.

Edit ONLY the image regions occupied by PEOPLE TO REMOVE and the background immediately behind those removed people.

Use each person's position and description to identify the correct people.

Reconstruct only the background revealed after removing PEOPLE TO REMOVE.

Preserve all other original pixels, composition, buildings, vehicles, objects, lighting, colors, perspective, and image quality as closely as possible.

Do not add new people or objects.

Do not remove people shown only in posters, advertisements, photographs, paintings, statues, mannequins, screens, or other non-real representations.

Return only the edited photo.`

parameters.content:
## Photo Upload & Analysis

Receives one or more travel photos from the upload form.

Normalizes the form input, splits multiple uploads into individual photo items, and uses Gemini to detect real people in each image.

The analysis result is normalized before the workflow decides how each photo should be processed.

# AI Travel Photo Cleaner

## What this workflow does

This workflow removes unwanted people from one or more travel photos using AI image analysis and editing.

Users can upload multiple photos at once and choose whether to remove all detected people or keep selected people in each photo.

The workflow detects real people in each image, skips unnecessary AI editing when no people are found, processes only the photos that require editing, and returns the results in the original photo order.

## Features

- Upload and process multiple photos at once
- AI-powered real person detection
- Remove all detected people from photos
- Keep selected people while removing others
- Skip AI editing when no people are detected
- Preserve the original order of uploaded photos
- Individual download links for each processed photo
- Japanese and English form support
- Temporary Google Drive storage for result delivery
- Automatic cleanup of temporary files after 24 hours

## Required Credentials

- Google Gemini API
- Google Drive OAuth2 API

## Required Workflow


## Setup

1. Configure the Google Gemini credentials used by the workflow.
2. Configure the Google Drive credentials used by the workflow.
3. Google Drive is used for temporary preview and result files. By default, files are stored in the root folder. You can optionally select a dedicated folder in the Google Drive upload nodes.
4. Ensure the Google Drive credential is also configured in the "Delete Temporary Photo" node.
5. Publish or activate the workflow.
6. Open the production form URL to start using the photo cleaner.

## How to test

1. Open the production photo upload form.
2. Select Japanese or English.
3. Upload one or more travel photos.
4. Choose whether to remove all people or keep selected people.
5. If keeping selected people, select the people you want to preserve for each photo.
6. Wait for the AI processing to complete.
7. Confirm that the processed photos are displayed in the original upload order.
8. Download each processed photo from the result page.
9. Confirm that temporary files are removed after the configured retention period.

## Notes

The workflow is designed to detect and remove real people physically present in the photographed scene.

People shown only in posters, advertisements, photographs, paintings, statues, mannequins, screens, or similar representations should not be treated as removable people.

AI image editing may produce different results depending on image complexity, overlapping subjects, lighting, and background details.

When a removed person significantly overlaps with a subject that should remain, AI may reconstruct parts of that subject or the surrounding scene.

Temporary preview and result files are stored in Google Drive and scheduled for automatic deletion after 24 hours.

## Processing Route

Checks whether real people were detected in each photo and routes the photo to the appropriate processing path.

Photos with no detected people are preserved without AI editing.

For photos containing people, the workflow follows the selected mode: remove all detected people or keep selected people while removing the others.

## People Selection & Selective Removal

Prepares previews for photos containing detected people and displays a selection form so the user can choose which people to keep.

The selected people are preserved while unselected people are removed with AI image editing.

Multiple photos are processed independently so different people can be kept in each photo.

## Remove All People

Removes all detected real people from photos using AI image editing.

The edited image is prepared for merging with photos from the other processing paths.

## Preserve Unchanged Photos

Preserves photos when no real people are detected.

These photos skip AI image editing and are passed directly to the final result, avoiding unnecessary processing and maintaining the original image.

## Result Delivery

Merges photos from all processing paths and restores them to their original upload order.

Uploads the final images to temporary Google Drive storage and generates individual download links for each processed photo.

Displays the completed results in the form with photo previews, download links, and the temporary file retention notice.

## Temporary File Cleanup

Collects the temporary Google Drive files created for previews and result delivery.

Waits 24 hours and then deletes these temporary files from Google Drive, helping prevent unnecessary files from remaining in storage.
